q: Chemistry is an area of knowledge remarkable for its breadth and ____.
e: Chemistry encompasses a wide range of topics and detailed scientific principles.

q: Knowledge of chemistry is essential to improve the quality of our ____.
e: Chemical innovations lead to better medicines, materials, and technologies that enhance daily living.

q: Faster electronic devices, stronger plastics, and more effective medicines and vaccines all rely on the innovations of ____ throughout the world.
e: Chemists are the scientists responsible for developing new materials and medical treatments.

q: We cannot truly understand or even know very much about the world we live in or about our own bodies without knowing the fundamental concepts of ____.
e: Chemistry provides the foundational knowledge required to understand matter and biological processes.

q: ____, water contamination, air pollution, food shortages and other societal issues are regularly featured in the media.
e: Climate change is a major global societal issue where chemistry plays a crucial role in finding solutions.

q: Climate change, ____, air pollution, food shortages and other societal issues are regularly featured in the media.
e: Water contamination is a critical environmental challenge addressed through chemical analysis and treatment.

q: Climate change, water contamination, ____, food shortages and other societal issues are regularly featured in the media.
e: Air pollution involves chemical contaminants in the atmosphere, requiring chemical solutions for mitigation.

q: Climate change, water contamination, air pollution, ____ and other societal issues are regularly featured in the media.
e: Food shortages are linked to agricultural chemistry and the development of fertilizers and pesticides.

q: As the '____', chemistry is woven into the fabric of practically every issue that our society faces today.
e: Chemistry connects with physics, biology, and environmental science to address complex societal problems.

q: The usual definition is that chemistry is a study of ____ and the changes it undergoes.
e: Matter is anything that has mass and occupies space, and chemistry focuses on its properties and transformations.

q: What is matter? It is anything that has ____ and occupies space.
e: Mass is a fundamental property of matter, distinguishing it from energy or empty space.

q: We change matter to make it more ____.
e: Chemical processes are applied to raw materials to create products that serve human needs.

q: Some matter we change to extract a part of its energy; for example, we burn ____ to get energy to propel our automobiles.
e: Gasoline undergoes combustion, a chemical reaction that releases energy for mechanical work.

q: We practice chemistry when we cook in the kitchen, when we clean our house or paint our room, when we apply ____, and when we take medicine or treat an injury.
e: Cosmetics involve chemical formulations designed for personal care and appearance.

q: Our body takes ____ from the air and combines it with part of the food we eat to provide us with energy for every activity we undertake.
e: Oxygen is essential for cellular respiration, the process that generates energy in living organisms.

q: It deals with matter from the tiniest parts of ____ to the complex human body.
e: Atoms are the basic building blocks of all matter, forming the foundation of chemical study.

q: Prehistoric time to the beginning of Christian era (about 300 BC) is classified as ____ period.
e: This early period involved mystical beliefs about matter before the establishment of scientific methods.

q: The ancients believed the world made of '____', which are earth, air, water and fire.
e: This was an early philosophical concept to explain the composition of the natural world.

q: The ____ were perhaps the first to formulate theories explaining the behaviour of matter without confirming their theories by experimentation.
e: Early Greek thinkers relied on logic and observation rather than controlled experiments.

q: Their philosophic point of view of nature, which can be attributed mainly to ____, dominated the Greek culture.
e: Aristotle's ideas about the four elements and nature heavily influenced early scientific thought.

q: From about 300 BC to the end of 17th century, the experimental roots of chemistry are planted in ____, a mystical chemistry that flourished in China and Europe.
e: Alchemy was a proto-scientific tradition that combined chemistry, metallurgy, and mysticism.

q: Alchemists made several attempts to turn cheaper metals to gold, using the substance called the ____.
e: The Philosopher's Stone was a legendary alchemical substance believed to enable transmutation of metals.

q: They also wanted to find an ____ that would enable people to live longer and cure all ailments.
e: The elixir of life was a mythical potion sought by alchemists for immortality and healing.

q: They also wanted to find an elixir that would enable people to live longer and cure all ____.
e: Alchemists sought universal remedies to heal any disease or physical ailment.

q: In 1661 ____ developed the basic ideas about the behaviour of gases.
e: Robert Boyle is often considered one of the founders of modern chemistry, particularly for his work on gas laws.

q: Traditional chemistry period started by the end of 17th century up to the middle of ____ century.
e: This period marked the transition from alchemy to a more systematic, experimental science.

q: In 1774 ____ discovered a gas, later named oxygen.
e: Joseph Priestley's discovery of oxygen was a pivotal moment in the history of chemistry.

q: Chemistry was introduced to the science in 1768 by French chemist ____, who explained the law of conservation of matter based on the experimentation method.
e: Lavoisier is known as the 'father of modern chemistry' for establishing the law of conservation of mass.

q: From this onward, scientists use the experimentation method, also known as ____, rather than logical and theoretical method of the ancients.
e: The scientific method relies on empirical evidence, hypothesis testing, and reproducibility.

q: In 1803 ____ postulated Atomic Theory, which states that all matter is composed of atoms, which are small and indivisible.
e: Dalton's Atomic Theory provided a foundational framework for understanding chemical reactions and matter.

q: ____ laid the groundwork for a more quantitative approach to chemistry by calculating the number of particles in a given amount of a gas, which we use today as Avogadro's constant.
e: Avogadro's hypothesis was crucial for determining molecular weights and stoichiometry.

q: Modern chemistry starts from the middle of 19th century to the ____ time.
e: Modern chemistry is characterized by advanced instrumentation, quantum mechanics, and diverse specialized branches.

q: Scientific facts remain the same, no matter who does the ____.
e: Objectivity and reproducibility are core tenets of the scientific method.

q: Few of the areas that have emerged as being especially important in modern chemistry are Synthesis, Separation techniques, Identification and assay, Materials, Polymers, ____, Biochemistry, Molecular biology, Green chemistry, and Combinatorial chemistry.
e: Nanochemistry deals with the synthesis and characterization of materials at the nanoscale.

q: Examples of early chemical changes include: extraction of metals from ____, making pottery and glazes, fermenting beer and wine, extracting chemicals from plants for medicine and perfume, making of fat into soap, manufacture of glass, and making of alloys like bronze and so on.
e: Extracting metals from ores was one of the earliest practical applications of chemical processes by ancient civilizations.

q: Examples of early chemical changes include: extraction of metals from ores, making pottery and ____, fermenting beer and wine, extracting chemicals from plants for medicine and perfume, making of fat into soap, manufacture of glass, and making of alloys like bronze and so on.
e: Glazes are glassy coatings applied to pottery, created through high-temperature chemical reactions.

q: Examples of early chemical changes include: extraction of metals from ores, making pottery and glazes, fermenting beer and ____, extracting chemicals from plants for medicine and perfume, making of fat into soap, manufacture of glass, and making of alloys like bronze and so on.
e: Fermentation is a biochemical process used since ancient times to produce alcoholic beverages like beer and wine.

q: Examples of early chemical changes include: extraction of metals from ores, making pottery and glazes, fermenting beer and wine, extracting chemicals from plants for medicine and ____, making of fat into soap, manufacture of glass, and making of alloys like bronze and so on.
e: Ancient cultures extracted aromatic chemicals from plants to create perfumes and medicinal remedies.

q: Examples of early chemical changes include: extraction of metals from ores, making pottery and glazes, fermenting beer and wine, extracting chemicals from plants for medicine and perfume, making of fat into ____, manufacture of glass, and making of alloys like bronze and so on.
e: The saponification process, turning fat into soap, is an early example of a practical chemical reaction.

q: Examples of early chemical changes include: extraction of metals from ores, making pottery and glazes, fermenting beer and wine, extracting chemicals from plants for medicine and perfume, making of fat into soap, manufacture of ____, and making of alloys like bronze and so on.
e: Glass manufacture involves melting silica and other minerals, representing an early mastery of high-temperature chemistry.

q: Examples of early chemical changes include: extraction of metals from ores, making pottery and glazes, fermenting beer and wine, extracting chemicals from plants for medicine and perfume, making of fat into soap, manufacture of glass, and making of alloys like ____ and so on.
e: Bronze is an alloy of copper and tin, marking a significant advancement in early metallurgical chemistry.

q: Alchemists never achieved these goals, but they discovered many new chemical substances and techniques such as ____ and extraction that are still used today.
e: Distillation is a separation technique pioneered by alchemists that remains fundamental in modern chemistry.

q: Alchemists never achieved these goals, but they discovered many new chemical substances and techniques such as distillation and ____ that are still used today.
e: Extraction is a method used to separate desired substances from a mixture, developed during the alchemical period.

q: Chemical reactions occur when you breathe, eat, or just sit there ____.
e: Even passive activities involve metabolic chemical reactions within the body.

q: The air you are breathing is a mixture of elements like ____ and nitrogen.
e: Oxygen is a vital component of the Earth's atmosphere, essential for respiration.

q: The book you are reading is made from wood pulp or ____ which has been bleached and treated with various chemicals.
e: Cellulose is a natural polymer found in plant cell walls, used extensively in paper production.

q: The clothes you are wearing are probably made from synthetic chemicals called ____, such as nylon or terylene.
e: Synthetic polymers are large molecules manufactured for use in textiles and plastics.

q: The seat you are sitting on is perhaps a plastic polymer, with ____; foam seat padding and metal support.
e: Polyurethane is a versatile polymer commonly used in foam padding for furniture.

q: The room you are in is made from cement, plastics, concrete and ____, all of which are chemicals.
e: Glass is an amorphous solid material, typically made from silica, and is a product of chemical processing.

q: Some chemicals are ____.
e: Toxic chemicals can cause harm to living organisms, highlighting the need for safe handling.

q: All matter is made of chemicals, so the importance of chemistry is that it is the study of ____.
e: Since all physical substances are composed of chemicals, chemistry is fundamentally the study of all matter.

q: The five main branches are considered to be Organic chemistry, Inorganic chemistry, Physical chemistry, Analytical chemistry, and ____.
e: Biochemistry focuses on the chemical processes and substances occurring within living organisms.

q: In addition, Nuclear chemistry, Environmental chemistry, Industrial chemistry, Polymer chemistry, Materials chemistry, Nanochemistry, Green chemistry, Agricultural chemistry, Theoretical chemistry, etc., are other branches of ____.
e: The field of chemistry is highly diverse, with numerous specialized branches addressing specific types of matter and applications.

q: In addition, Nuclear chemistry, ____ chemistry, Industrial chemistry, Polymer chemistry, Materials chemistry, Nanochemistry, Green chemistry, Agricultural chemistry, Theoretical chemistry, etc., are other branches of chemistry.
e: Environmental chemistry studies the chemical and biochemical phenomena that occur in natural places.

q: In addition, Nuclear chemistry, Environmental chemistry, Industrial chemistry, Polymer chemistry, Materials chemistry, Nanochemistry, Green chemistry, ____ chemistry, Theoretical chemistry, etc., are other branches of chemistry.
e: Agricultural chemistry deals with the chemical processes involved in crop production and soil management.

q: Organic chemistry is the study of most carbon-containing chemicals which are hydrocarbons and their ____.
e: Derivatives are compounds formed from hydrocarbons by replacing one or more hydrogen atoms with other functional groups.

q: Inorganic chemistry is the study of, in general, matter that does not deal with ____.
e: Inorganic chemistry typically covers minerals, metals, and non-metals, excluding carbon-based hydrocarbons.

q: Physical chemistry is the study of the behaviour and changes of matter and the related ____ changes.
e: Physical chemistry applies physics principles to understand the energy dynamics of chemical reactions.

q: Analytical chemistry is the study of components and ____ of substances.
e: Analytical chemistry focuses on identifying and quantifying the chemical makeup of materials.

q: Biochemistry is the study of matter and processes of ____ organisms.
e: Biochemistry bridges biology and chemistry to understand life at a molecular level.

q: Physical chemistry is the study of the behaviour and changes of matter and the related energy changes, such as reaction rates and reaction ____.
e: Reaction mechanisms describe the step-by-step sequence of elementary reactions by which overall chemical change occurs.

q: Analytical chemistry is the study of components and compositions of substances, including food nutrients, quality control (QC) and quality ____ (QA).
e: Quality assurance ensures that products meet specified requirements and standards through analytical testing.

q: Biochemistry is the study of matter and processes of living organisms, such as metabolism and ____.
e: Fermentation is a metabolic process that produces chemical changes in organic substrates through the action of enzymes.

q: Inorganic chemistry is the study of, in general, matter that does not deal with hydrocarbons, such as minerals, metals and non-metals, and ____.
e: Semi-conductors are inorganic materials crucial for modern electronics and digital technology.

q: By studying and understanding chemistry, you will become a global citizen in the ____ first century.
e: Chemical literacy is essential for navigating the complex scientific and environmental challenges of the 21st century.

q: The principles of chemistry are needed to understand the nature of every form of ____.
e: Chemical principles dictate the properties and behaviors of all physical substances.

q: For example, metals, drugs, gasoline, foods, the earth's crust, water, atmosphere, radioactive materials and the human brain cell, all have properties determined mainly by ____ principles.
e: The behavior of diverse materials and biological systems is governed by underlying chemical rules.

q: Consumer aspects of chemistry and the chemistry of common things can also be known from the fundamental ideas of ____.
e: Basic chemical concepts help consumers understand the products they use daily.

q: Chemistry has helped in establishing industries which manufacture utility goods, such as acids, alkalis, soaps, ____, dyes, polymers, metals, etc.
e: Detergents are synthetic cleaning agents developed through chemical engineering.

q: These industries contribute in a big way to the ____ of a nation and generate employment.
e: The chemical industry is a major driver of economic growth and job creation.

q: Chemistry is also required for many fields of ____.
e: A foundation in chemistry is a prerequisite for advanced studies in medicine, pharmacy, and engineering.

q: For example, courses in Pharmacy and ____ require applicants to have knowledge of chemistry; cutting-edge of today's digital technology requires knowledge on the principles of chemistry.
e: Medicine requires a deep understanding of chemistry to comprehend drug interactions and human physiology.

q: Chemistry is considered as an ____ science.
e: Chemistry relies on empirical data gathered through controlled laboratory experiments.

q: You should recognise that the principles and laws of nature are the results of extensive observations and speculative analyses refined over many ____.
e: Scientific laws are established through repeated testing and validation over time.

q: Basic process skills such as observing, classifying, inferring, communicating, measuring, predicting and using numbers will be developed if you study ____.
e: Studying chemistry cultivates essential scientific skills applicable to various disciplines.

q: Basic process skills such as observing, classifying, inferring, communicating (through diagram, graph, chart, etc.), measuring, predicting and using ____ will be developed if you study chemistry.
e: Quantitative skills, including the use of numbers, are essential for chemical calculations and data analysis.

q: You are expected to enhance the development of these skills and use them to construct your chemical knowledge, and hence engage in ____ learning.
e: Science education aims to foster continuous learning and adaptation throughout an individual's life.

q: Agriculture also uses chemistry in many areas, and it is very important for the food and beverage industry and ____ industry.
e: The medical industry relies on chemistry for the discovery, development, and production of pharmaceuticals.

q: Basic chemistry is the branch of science that studies the preparation, properties, structures and ____ of material substances.
e: Chemical reactions involve the transformation of substances into new materials with different properties.

q: Basic chemistry is the branch of science that studies the preparation, properties, structures and reactions of material ____.
e: Material substances are the physical matter that chemistry seeks to understand and manipulate.

q: Chemistry contributes to a large extent in the development and growth of a ____.
e: Scientific and industrial advancement in chemistry directly supports national development.

q: A developing country, like Myanmar, needs talented and creative ____.
e: Skilled chemists are vital for solving local environmental, medical, and industrial challenges.

q: To be a good chemist, one needs to understand the basic concepts of ____.
e: A strong grasp of foundational concepts is necessary for advanced chemical research and application.

q: On this context, there are six main themes in Basic Education High School Chemistry Course: Particulate nature of substances, Periodicity, Chemical calculations, Chemistry of reactions, the Environment and ____ chemistry.
e: Organic chemistry is a core theme, focusing on carbon-based compounds and their reactions.

q: Knowledge of these chemistry principles will help you to better understand the ____ and hazards to mankind and enable you to make intelligent decisions in the future.
e: Chemistry provides numerous advantages to society, which must be balanced against potential risks.

q: Knowledge of these chemistry principles will help you to better understand the benefits and hazards to mankind and enable you to make intelligent decisions in the ____.
e: Understanding chemistry empowers individuals to make informed choices about health, environment, and technology.
